name: Pacivrel
description: Pacivrel is a selective aggression inhibitor targeting the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and orbital frontal cortex circuits associated with reactive anger and impulsive aggression. It does not suppress assertiveness, self-defense capacity, or emotional expressiveness broadly — it specifically dampens the neural cascade that converts frustration into rage. Prescribed for anger disorders, domestic violence rehabilitation programs, and mandatory chemical compliance for individuals on conditional release.
effects: suppression of reactive anger and rage responses
side_effects: in some users, suppressed anger re-routes as passive aggression, resentment, or depression
reduces appropriate protective anger — users may fail to respond adequately to genuine threats
when used as mandatory compliance medication, associated with psychological resistance and resentment
withdrawal anger spikes that can be severe
some users report feeling 'hollow' — anger was a significant part of their emotional identity
cultural_context: Pacivrel has two distinct cultural identities. In Tier 3-4, it's a voluntary lifestyle medication — people take it before difficult conversations, family gatherings, or high-stress work days. In Tier 1-2, it's frequently court-mandated, administered as a condition of parole or shelter access, and carries the social weight of state control. Shelf residents call mandatory Pacivrel programs 'the muzzle' — a tool to keep poor people docile while their conditions remain unchanged. The irony that the city's most legitimately angry population is the one most frequently compelled to suppress that anger is not lost on anyone. Novafold's profit margins on mandatory compliance contracts are among its highest.
story_hooks: A Shelf community leader has been on mandatory Pacivrel for two years after a conviction — she's become a model of calm, measured advocacy. She's just found a way off it legally, and she's terrified of who she'll be when the anger comes back.

A Tier 4 executive is voluntarily taking Pacivrel to manage his temper during a hostile takeover — but his board is using his chemically induced passivity to push through decisions he'd never have agreed to at baseline.

Someone is lacing the water supply in a specific Shelf zone with Pacivrel ahead of a planned demolition and displacement. The residents keep meaning to organize resistance and keep finding it hard to feel urgent about it.
